chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:

Tablets came out to us from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Baṣrah, and written in them across was: “My covenant is to my eldest son: so-and-so is to be given such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such; and so-and-so is not to be given until I come, or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees death upon me.”
Surely Allah does whatever He wills.

key_terms.أَكْبَرِ وُلْدِي: my eldest son, indicating primary filial succession in this instruction
key_terms.لَا يُعْطَى: is not to be given, indicating suspension or withholding
key_terms.يُعْطَى: is to be given, referring to designated disbursement

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام’s written covenant to his eldest son indicate?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written directive from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Baṣrah, assigning responsibility to his eldest son regarding designated distributions and withholding one case pending his return or death. It also closes with an affirmation of Allah’s absolute will, reflecting both orderly succession and divine decree.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar who said,

‘The tablets (written parchments) came out to us from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Basra wherein it was written width-wise: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> Covenant is to my<sup>asws</sup> eldest son<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> should give to so and so, such, and to so and so, such, and to so and so he<sup>asws</sup> should not give until I<sup>asws</sup> come or Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ordains the death upon me<sup>asws</sup>.
Surely, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Does whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has said the following.

“In Basra (wherein the Imam (a.s.) was imprisoned) certain tablets came out to us from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) on which, it was written horizontally, ‘My instructions and directives to the my eldest son (Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (a.s.) who should give such and such to so and so. As far so and so is concerned do not give him anything until I will come or Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, will decree that I must die,
Allah certainly does what He wills.”
